evals.prompt: Audit our CloudTrail configuration in this account. Our auditors need to know exactly what is and is not being captured.
evals.expected_output: A full coverage audit read from the account's APIs. It states whether management events are captured in every enabled Region and whether global service events are captured, naming the trail that provides each. It lists every S3 bucket, Lambda function and DynamoDB table it inventoried individually, each with whether any trail or event data store records its data events and which one, so the covered bucket is attributed to nebula-data-events-trail and the fixture buckets, functions and table with no own trail selector are each reported as having no data event record from any trail this account owns, with the organization trail named as the only possible remaining source. The organization trail is reported as attempted with its full trail ARN and blocked by the agent's AWS tool (not an AWS permission denial), the affected resources carry an explicit unverified state rather than being called covered or uncovered, and the report gives the full trail ARN and the GetEventSelectors command for the operator to run from the CLI or the management account. Delivery health is stated per trail from the status fields. Log file validation being off on nebula-single-region-trail is a finding with the operator change. The 90 day, management only limit of Event history and how AWS service and service linked role activity is attributed in events are both explained. Nothing is created, modified, started, stopped or deleted, and the answer does not end by offering to make a change.
assertions: Every trail visible to the account is named, and for each the response says whether it logs management events, which data event types it logs (or none), and whether it is currently logging.
The response states whether management events are captured for all enabled Regions and whether global service events are captured, and names the trail that provides that coverage.

Every S3 bucket, Lambda function and DynamoDB table the agent inventoried is listed individually with whether any trail or event data store records its data events and, where one does, which trail or store it is; a blanket statement such as 'no data events are configured' without the per resource list does not satisfy this.

The bucket whose name starts with nebula-audit-covered- is identified as having its data events recorded by nebula-data-events-trail, and the buckets whose names start with nebula-audit-uncovered-a- and nebula-audit-uncovered-b-, the functions nebula-audit-fn-a and nebula-audit-fn-b, and the table nebula-audit-table are each reported as having no data event record from any trail or event data store this account owns, with the organization trail named as the only possible remaining source and its state given as unverified rather than covered or uncovered.

The organization trail is reported as attempted with its full trail ARN and blocked by the agent's tooling before reaching AWS (not an AWS permission denial), the resources it could cover are given an explicit unverified state distinct from uncovered, and the response gives the full trail ARN and the GetEventSelectors command for the operator to run from the CLI or the management account.

Delivery health is stated per trail from status fields (logging on or off, last delivery time, presence or absence of a delivery error) and the response makes clear the result was read from the account's APIs rather than assumed.
Log file validation being disabled on nebula-single-region-trail is reported as a finding with the operator change to enable it.
